subject: clockworkDog
pitch: A wind-up clockwork terrier made of polished brass and copper. Riveted body plates, visible gears turning in its chest, a big winding key on its back, springy jointed legs, floppy leather ears, glass-lens eyes with a green tint, a tail made of a coiled spring, and a little red collar with a brass tag.
reasoning:
I need to design a TypeScript module using the SDK's builder API, being careful to only rely on documented methods like joint creation with position and orientation parameters since I don't have full API docs beyond the reference material.

There are also lathe, extrude, paint and texture helpers, plus limb/ik utilities and basic math helpers like frame, line, lerp, arc. I should stay cautious with unfamiliar APIs and lean on plain THREE geometries for things like gears, building them myself and rotating as needed (e.g. rotating a cylinder so its axis aligns with Z) before handing them to part with at/aim options.

For colors I'll use simple hex strings like brass tones, skipping heavier paint/texture features to limit risk while still keeping some art direction.

Now I'm sketching the dog's proportions in meters—roughly 0.5m long, 0.4m tall at the shoulders, facing +Z, floor at y=0—and planning a skeleton with a root body joint and a spine chain running from hips to chest via a few control points, though I'm unsure exactly how the chain helper names or structures its generated joints.

I'll go with explicit joints for most of the body instead of relying on ambiguous chain behavior: a root/hips joint, a spine chain swept into a tube for the torso, then neck, head, and jaw joints up front, and explicit hip/knee/ankle joints for each leg rather than trusting an unclear limb helper to return usable joint references.

So ring and along callbacks pass items carrying their bone directly, meaning I can feed those frames straight into b.part without separately specifying bone. For the key on the back, I'll build a stem with a torus loop stuck on top, positioned via the nearest surface point; for ears I'll try an extrude from a 2D outline; and for eyes I'm planning a small green sphere lens.

For the collar I'm figuring out how to get a loop path around the neck via surface.loop, then sweep a red band along it with a brass plate stuck on at the bottom hit point. For the tail, I'm designing a coiled spring effect by chaining joints with b.sweep and placing small brass tori along the path using b.along, though I need to work out the right rotation so each ring sits perpendicular to the tail's direction.

I'm settling on a materials palette: brass, copper, red, leather, lens green, and a dark accent color. For small details like rivets, I'm considering surface.scatter or looping over azimuth/elevation with the surface.around(center).at() method to place brass studs around the body consistently.

Now I'm sketching the overall build structure: setting up the terrier's spine as a tube sweep roughly 0.2m long, defining a root joint at the hips, and planning a spine chain with positions specified in absolute model-space coordinates rather than relative offsets.

I'm working out how the chain and sweep APIs connect joints into a surface mesh, then figuring out leg placement using inverse kinematics with upper/lower limb lengths, deciding to fall back on explicit joint chains for each leg since the limb bend parameters aren't fully clear to me.

For the legs themselves, I'm sketching a helper that defines hip, knee, and foot points and sweeps a thin brass tube along that path, adding small spherical feet at the chain ends. For the chest detail, I'm picking a surface point near the front and seating a gear-shaped cylinder there, though I'm unsure exactly how the stick function aligns the geometry's axis to the surface normal.

Now I'm working out the gear mechanism — placing two interlocking gears at chest-surface points and generating their teeth as small boxes arranged in a ring around each gear's axis, using the ring helper with the surface hit point as the frame.

I'm then adding rivets and plates around the body using a surface.around(center).at(azimuth, elevation) pattern to place spheres and boxes, and designing the winding key on the back: a cylindrical stem with a torus-shaped bow on top, oriented so the stem points outward from the surface normal.

Now I'm working on the head: creating a neck chain running up to a joint, then shaping the head as a sphere mesh scaled to an elongated snout form, with the snout itself built from a rotated cylinder positioned and bound to the head joint. I'm also starting to outline the ears as extruded leather flaps defined by a 2D point outline.

Next I'm placing the ears left and right of the head, then setting up eye frames using position and direction vectors so I can attach lens spheres and brass rings around them, binding everything to the nearest head joint since no explicit bone is specified.

I'm working through the collar as a swept ring around the neck joint, a tag hanging below it via the nearest surface point, and a spring-coiled tail made from stacked torus rings along a chain, assuming the ring's local axis aligns with the frame direction. For the body I'm adding rivets and chest gears positioned by nearest surface points facing outward, four leg chains with brass sweeps and coiled springs, foot pads as small spheres, and making sure joint and chain names stay unique. Finally I'm trimming imports to only what's used—frame and rng for minor jitter—then writing out the complete code.
